explanation: No single theme. The strongest repeated case is ' with' in the Apache license phrase 'use this file except in compliance with the License'. Otherwise it fires on unrelated tokens: Seq in a config key, Sandy, a birth-date space, 'pose', URL pieces ('https', 'symlinks', 'bypass'), place-name fragments and others.

Fires on assorted function and modifier words that continue a phrase: 'new' (new password, new album, Java 'new'), 'even', 'including' (in patent phrasing), 'of'/'to'/'with' in boilerplate, 'wrong'. There is no clear shared meaning, though 'new' and 'even' recur at the top.

A mixture. The clearest repeated case is ' permission' in the BSD license phrase 'without specific prior written permission'. Other hits are unrelated: code and identifier fragments ('.jpg', '=localhost', 'Identifier'), word-final pieces such as 'RELEVANCE' and 'representation', and the paragraph break after a sentence.

Fires on words that describe two parties being related, joined or separated: 'parted ways', 'tied the knot', 'remained friends', 'double date', 'sever ties', 'both sides', 'closely related', 'joined', 'interlink', 'hybridized', 'the other team'. It fires most when the context says 'the two' or 'both'.

Fires on the second token of a common fixed compound or collocation, the token that completes it: Sold Out, Breakdown, input data, Minimum wage, Login, copy & paste, sign in/into, Silicon Valley, Best Buy, My Page, testSerialization. It responds to the predictability of the completion more than to any topic.

Fires on digits and decimal points inside numbers, mostly decimals in statistics and measurements. It is strongest on the digit right after the decimal point or on the '.' itself, as in percentages and means ('41.4%', '0.69978'); a DOI digit is the top hit. Integer digits fire more weakly.

Mixed. Many top hits are inner word-pieces of multi-token medical or technical words ('incontinence', 'thromboembolism', 'progenitor', 'deacetylase', 'Kaplan-Meier') and fragments of legal citations or codes ('cv', '501(c)', 'B.R.', 'No. 02'). Other hits are unrelated function words ('this', 'that', 'gone') and the space before a number.

Fires mainly in clinical and biomedical case-report text, on the clinical finding or measurement term: 'weakness', 'paralysis', 'pain', 'expiratory volume', 'fragment length', 'left knee', 'revealed a', '99mTc'. A few hits are field or attribute names in code ('date attribute', 'POST').

Fires on the token that starts a clause or turns the sentence in a new direction, often an existential 'there'/'There' ('There is/are', 'see there is') or a contrast ('The bad news', 'without', 'unless', 'not limited to'). It fires where the sentence is about to state a new fact or a qualification.

Fires on a header or boilerplate end-point where a document's introduction ends: the project name in 'This file is part of the X project/Framework' (FreeType, Nette, Swift.org), the double newline after a date heading in blog posts, the include-guard name after #define, and 'I am new to C++'. It responds to header or title lines that come right before the main text begins.

Fires inside LaTeX math, mostly on closing braces '}' that end a fraction, exponent or subscript group, and on '\frac' or '\in' and subscript indices. Dollar signs before money amounts fire moderately.

Mixed. It fires on negators or quantifiers in 'no one'/'no modern president'/'could not', determiners such as 'these' and 'one', commas after an introductory phrase, and chemistry or lab terms ('C-C bond', 'acrylic resin', 'SDS-PAGE', 'mass spectrometry'). No single function stands out.

Mostly fires on the first word-piece after the start of a multi-token rare word or proper name, so the rest of the word is predictable: Apodemus, Chunsheng, ILLINOIS, TORONTO, nucleoside, cesarean, activating, adenine, harrier, Marlon. A few function-word hits ('was', 'can', 'in') don't fit.

Fires on the starting word-piece of a split word, especially 'Fr'/'FR' (Franson, FRANCISCO, Fray, fructify, frickin, Fracking, Frankenstein) and similar onsets such as 'Ots', 'Pr', 'Rapt', 'nalt', in names and drug or chemical terms.

Fires on the word-piece 'Pro'/'pro'/'PRO' at the start of a multi-token word (Protests, Problems, Procrastination, Progesterone, Procedural, prophylaxis, PROHIBITED, procesamos, Prozentsatz). Weaker hits come from similar onsets such as 'prox', 'pr', 'rop' and 'RO'.

Fires on inner word-pieces of compound technical or lab-method terms, mostly the second half of a hyphenated or fused compound: 'in situ hybridization', 'X-ray', 'gas chromatography', 'immunosorbent', 'photosensitive', 'surface-mountable', 'microextraction', 'saltwater'. It is strongest in patent or scientific methods text.

Mostly sports-statistics context: tokens in player records and stat lines ('passing' yards, first Grade 'appearance', 'played for', 42 'points', '16-down', 'on-ice'). A separate group is notation tokens in numeric or statistical text: '+/-' in mean±SD, 'ldots' in math, '[1,' in arrays.

Fires on the second word of a technical or fixed compound term, often in code or domain jargon: greatest/lowest 'common' divisor/multiple, Glasgow Com'a', MINRES, appenders, default 'constructor', s3 'sync', layout_margin, ground 'floor', pulsed-field 'gel', Neurofeedback. It responds to completing a known multi-word technical name.

Mixed. It fires on the 'B' in bracketed citations '[@B8]', on name and word fragments (OVH, protozoan, WordPress, Stratosphere, Merrill Lynch, cirrhotic), and on unrelated ordinary words ('closed', 'previous', 'especially', 'your', 'version').

Mixed. It fires on 'just' in the sense of 'merely / yet' ('answer questions just because', 'just yet', 'just in case'), on digits in legal statute citations (28 U.S.C. § 2254, §§ 9541), and on scattered nouns ('percent', 'crimes', 'privilege', 'people').

Fires mostly in programming and technical-error contexts on the key noun or verb of the error or description ('SQL syntax', 'ERROR: function', 'cannot load', 'unused_imports', 'Subsystem', 'installed'). The top hit, 'data unit', is about data terms, and there are a few unrelated general hits ('depending', 'citizenship', 'variables').
